title: Strict scalar Hom identification and normalized evaluation square
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $\varphi:R	o S$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, $E=S\otimes_R-$ the sheafified ordinary scalar extension and $U$ restriction [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Extend them termwise to unbounded complexes. Use the actual product Hom complex and local evaluation [def-pur-hom-complex] [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]. There are natural chain isomorphisms $
u_A:S\otimes_R A\xrightarrow{\sim}UEA$ and $	heta_{P,N}:U\mathcal Hom_S^ ullet(EP,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom_R^ ullet(P,UN)$, with $
u(s\otimes x)=s\otimes x$ and $	heta(g)(x)=g(1\otimes x)$ on every slice and homogeneous component. For any $R$-complexes $P,J$, any $S$-complex $N$ and chain map $q:EJ	o N$, there is a unique $S$-linear chain map $\sigma_q:E\mathcal Hom_R^ ullet(P,J)	o\mathcal Hom_S^ ullet(EP,N)$ satisfying $\sigma_q(s\otimes f)(t\otimes p)=st\,q(1\otimes f(p))$. Put $\alpha_S(s\otimes f)(p)=s\otimes f(p)$. The strict equality $	heta_{P,N}\,U(\sigma_q)\,
u_{\mathcal Hom(P,J)}=\mathcal Hom_R(P,Uq)\,\mathcal Hom_R(P,
u_J)\,\alpha_S$ holds before localization. All maps commute with maps of the input complexes and compatible changes of coefficient rings and of $q$. No flatness, boundedness or K-injectivity is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03CZ (sites-modules-lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict), applied on each slice; agent extension to product Hom complexes and the scalar evaluation square.

proof.text: Work throughout with the underlying sheaves of abelian groups and their given module actions. On the localized site $\mathcal C/W$, restriction of scalars is sectionwise restriction along $R|_W\to S|_W$. The tensor-restriction isomorphism identifies $(EA)|_W$ with $S|_W\otimes_{R|_W}(A|_W)$ and sends every sheafification-unit image of $s\otimes x$ to that same generator. It respects the $S|_W$-action: multiplication by a local scalar agrees on each presheaf generator, hence agrees on the sheafifications by their universal property. These identifications apply separately to every term of any complex. All generator calculations below are made over every object of every slice, followed by the sheafification universal property; they do not assert that every section of a sheaf tensor is a tensor of global sections.

source.place: Tag 03DH (section-localize); Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), applied to localization; Tag 03CY

proof.text: For module sheaves $A,B$ over any one of these slices, an $R$-linear sheaf map $h:A\to UB$ gives the sectionwise $S$-linear presheaf map $s\otimes x\mapsto s h(x)$ by the ordinary module scalar-Hom bijection. Restrictions commute with it since $(s h(x))|_Z=s|_Z h(x|_Z)$. Sheafification therefore extends it uniquely to $EA\to B$. Conversely $g:EA\to B$ gives $x\mapsto g(1\otimes x)$. The composites are identities: on $A$ this is $1h(x)=h(x)$; on the tensor presheaf it is $s g(1\otimes x)=g(s\otimes x)$, and equality passes uniquely to its sheafification. This proves the normalized slice adjunction used below, including its inverse formula, directly from the cited module bijection and sheafification. Precomposition, postcomposition, and further restriction commute with both formulas by substitution.

For each degree $i$, the $R$-sheaf $S\otimes_R A^i$ and $UE(A^i)$ have the same underlying abelian sheaf: both are the abelian sheafification of $W\mapsto S(W)\otimes_{R(W)}A^i(W)$. Module sheafification supplies the actions extending those on this presheaf; after restriction the two $R$-actions coincide. The identity on that presheaf induces mutually inverse $R$-linear maps by uniqueness of sheafification. This is $\nu_A^i$ and has the required value on generators. It commutes with the differential, since either composite sends $s\otimes x$ to $s\otimes d_Ax$, and is natural by the identical calculation with a map in place of $d_A$.

For integers $n,i$, a degree-$n$ section of $U\mathcal Hom_S^\bullet(EP,N)$ over $W$ is a family of $S|_W$-linear maps $(EP^i)|_W\to N^{i+n}|_W$. Apply the slice bijection of step 2 to each member. This gives the family $p\mapsto g^i(1\otimes p)$ in the actual product defining $\mathcal Hom_R^n(P,UN)(W)$. Its inverse takes a family $(h^i)_i$ to the maps $s\otimes p\mapsto s h^i(p)$, extended to the sheaf tensors as in step 2. They are inverse in every coordinate and commute with restriction, so define inverse maps of sheaves. Both are $R$-linear by their formulas. Thus they give the graded isomorphism $\theta$. This uses products of the coordinate bijections, not any preservation of products by $E$.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), product terms; sites-modules.tex Tag 03CZ on slices

proof.text: For a homogeneous family $g$ of degree $n$, the $i$-coordinate of $\theta(dg)$ evaluated at $p$ equals $d_N(g^i(1\otimes p))-(-1)^n g^{i+1}(1\otimes d_Pp)$, since $d_{EP}(1\otimes p)=1\otimes d_Pp$. This is exactly $(d\theta(g))^i(p)$. Equality of all coordinate sheaf maps proves the chain equation. The inverse graded isomorphism consequently also commutes with differentials. Thus $\theta$ is a chain isomorphism for unbounded complexes; no finite support condition on the family has been imposed.

Write $B=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,J)$. On a slice and in degrees $n,i$, the expression $(s,f,p)\mapsto s\otimes f^i(p)$ gives an $R$-balanced map in $(s,f)$ and an $R$-linear sheaf map in $p$. Indeed $\varphi(r)s\otimes f^i(p)=s\otimes r f^i(p)=s\otimes(rf)^i(p)$, and $f^i(rp)=r f^i(p)$. The tensor universal property followed by module sheafification gives, for each $i$, a map $S\otimes_R B^n\to\mathcal Hom_R(P^i,S\otimes_RJ^{i+n})$. Compatibility with slice restriction follows by restricting $s,f,p$ in the displayed formula. The product universal property assembles these maps into $\alpha_S^n$. Evaluating its differential at $p$ gives $s\otimes(d_J f^i(p)-(-1)^n f^{i+1}(d_Pp))$, which is $\alpha_S(s\otimes df)^i(p)$. Hence $\alpha_S$ is the asserted chain map. No exchange of tensor and product is used.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), product projections and differential; sites-modules.tex Tags 03CY and 03EL

proof.text: For a local homogeneous $f\in B^n(W)$, apply step 2 on $\mathcal C/W$ to the $R$-linear maps $p\mapsto q^{i+n}(1\otimes f^i(p))$. It gives the $S$-linear maps $t\otimes p\mapsto t q^{i+n}(1\otimes f^i(p))$ in every coordinate $i$. Their family is an element $b^n(f)$ of $\mathcal Hom_S^n(EP,N)(W)$. The formula is additive and $R$-linear in $f$ and commutes with restriction, so defines an $R$-linear sheaf map $b^n:B^n\to U\mathcal Hom_S^n(EP,N)$. Apply step 2 once more, now to $b^n$, to get the $S$-linear sheaf map $\sigma_q^n:E B^n\to\mathcal Hom_S^n(EP,N)$. Its $i$-coordinate on the prescribed generators is $(\sigma_q^n(s\otimes f))^i(t\otimes p)=st q^{i+n}(1\otimes f^i(p))$, as required.

The differential of $\sigma_q(s\otimes f)$ evaluated at $t\otimes p\in EP^i$ is $st[d_Nq^{i+n}(1\otimes f^i(p))-(-1)^n q^{i+n+1}(1\otimes f^{i+1}(d_Pp))]$. Since $q$ is a chain map, replace the first term by $q^{i+n+1}(1\otimes d_J f^i(p))$. The result is $st q^{i+n+1}(1\otimes (df)^i(p))$, the value of $\sigma_q(s\otimes df)$. Coordinatewise equality and uniqueness of sheafification prove the chain equation. If another $S$-linear map has the stated values, then for each local $s,f$ all its product coordinates agree with $\sigma_q$ on the tensor presheaf of $EP^i$; they agree on its sheafification. They then agree for every presheaf generator of $E B^n$, so again agree on its sheafification. This proves uniqueness.

Evaluate the two sides of the proposed square on a local $s\otimes f$ of degree $n$, in coordinate $i$ and at $p\in P^i$. The left side first leaves the tensor unchanged by $\nu_B$, then applies $\sigma_q$, then evaluates at $1\otimes p$ by $\theta$, giving $s q(1\otimes f^i(p))$. The right side gives successively $s\otimes f^i(p)$ by $\alpha_S$, that same generator in $UEJ$ by $\nu_J$, and $q(s\otimes f^i(p))$ by postcomposition. This equals the previous value by $S$-linearity of $q$. Equality of all Hom coordinates, followed by the tensor and sheafification universal properties in the source, proves the strict equality of chain maps. Evaluation here means the actual product projection followed by evaluation at the identity object of the slice, exactly the local convention in the cited representative-evaluation definition; its resolution choices are not used.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), product coordinates and componentwise composition; sites-modules.tex Tag 03CZ

proof.text: For chain maps $u:P'\to P$, $v:J\to J'$, $w:N\to N'$ with $q'\circ E v=w\circ q$, the two functorial composites involving $\sigma$ evaluate on $s\otimes f$, $t\otimes p'$ to $st q'(1\otimes v f(u(p')))$ and $w(st q(1\otimes f(u(p'))))$, respectively; these are equal by the displayed compatibility. The Hom action in the first variable is precomposition, so the direction of $u$ is contravariant. For $\theta$, pre- and postcomposition commute with $g\mapsto(p\mapsto g(1\otimes p))$ by direct substitution. For $\nu$ and $\alpha_S$ both naturality composites give respectively $s\otimes v(x)$ and $s\otimes v f(u(p'))$. The same generator-and-coordinate uniqueness arguments prove all these equalities as sheaf chain maps. Taking $u,v,w$ to be identities also proves naturality in $q$.

For coefficient compatibility, take a commuting square $a:R\to R'$, $b:S\to S'$, $\varphi':R'\to S'$ with $b\varphi=\varphi'a$. Put $P'=R'\otimes_RP$, $J'=R'\otimes_RJ$, $N'=S'\otimes_SN$. The canonical iterated-extension identifications send $s'\otimes(r'\otimes p)$ to $s'\varphi'(r')\otimes p$; the inverse inserts $1\otimes p$. Their relations and inverse equations follow from the tensor universal property and descend by sheafification. They give $q'$ by $q'(s'\otimes(r'\otimes j))=s'\varphi'(r')\otimes q(1\otimes j)$. The canonical Hom comparison sends $f$ to the family $f'(r'\otimes p)=r'\otimes f(p)$ (the construction in step 7 with $q$ the identity); analogous comparisons extend $S$-linear $g$ to $g'(s'\otimes z)=s'\otimes g(z)$. On generators, $\theta(g')$ and the extended $\theta(g)$ both send $1\otimes p$ to $1\otimes g(1\otimes p)$. For $\sigma$, both orders of change of coefficients send the images of $s\otimes f$ and $t\otimes p$ to $b(s)b(t)\otimes q(1\otimes f(p))$. For $\alpha$ and $\nu$ both orders send a tensor to that same tensor in the common extension. Linearity supplies arbitrary additional $R'$- and $S'$-scalars, and the two successive sheafification uniqueness arguments supply all sections. Thus the coefficient diagrams commute; no Hom comparison is claimed invertible. A tower is the same calculation with nested tensors; both bracketings multiply scalars in the same order, by associativity. If the target $N'$ is supplied with a compatible semilinear map instead of chosen as $S'\otimes_SN$, compose these equations with that map. This also includes compatible changes of $q$.
